newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BNDES seeks CVRD court order repeal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BNDES seeks CVRD court order repeal.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) is seeking to have a court order repealed which prevents investors from viewing information about soon-to-be-privatized state mining giant CVRD, a BNDES spokesman said.

Under the privatization rules for Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD), a so-called Data Room had been installed in the BNDES building in Rio de Janeiro to make information about the company available to interested investors.

The spokesman said the BNDES would be taking legal action in the federal courts against the order, arguing that the information in the Data Room was selected by CVRD itself and posed no threat to the company. The order was issued last week after deputy Luiz Gushiken of the Workers Party (PT) asked the courts to bar investors from gaining access to the Data Room.
The CVRD information center came under fire before it even opened its doors last Monday to register interested investors.
Days before, CVRD President Francisco Schettino expressed concern that the Data Room contained confidential information, disclosure of which could harm the company's business.
The BNDES spokesman said CVRD and the BNDES had resolved the issue and only displayed information in the Data Room which had been approved by CVRD.
He said the Data Room was closed at the moment, but was due to reopen next week when the first investors were scheduled to visit the facilities.
CVRD is to be privatized next year, with an initial 45-percent share block to go on sale in February, followed by a staff share offer and a public offer later in the year.
--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
